title: Company-wide policies and processes — consolidated reference
author: Aisha Patel
summary: This consolidated reference documents Redwood Inference’s company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for access and permissions, change management, data management, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel policies, and reusable internal templates. It is intended for all employees and managers to ensure consistent, auditable, and secure operations across teams.
introduction: Purpose: Standardize how Redwood manages access, changes to production systems, corporate data, third-party procurement, vendor engagements, and employee travel. Scope: Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors with access to company resources. Exceptions must be approved by the relevant policy owner and recorded in the related_pages list.
access_and_permissions:
Overview:
- Principle: least privilege by default; grant only the permissions required for an individual to perform their role.
- Access tiers:
  1) Corporate (HR/payroll/finance) — strictly limited and logged.
  2) Engineering (dev/test/prod) — segmented by environment and project.
  3) Customer data & PII — additional approval and encryption controls.
Roles & responsibilities:
- Manager: request and approve role-based access for new hires and contractors.
- IAM team: enforce RBAC, run quarterly entitlement reviews, and maintain role templates.
- Security: perform annual access audits and investigate anomalies.
Provisioning procedure (numbered):
1. Manager submits access request via the Access Request form (internal link).
2. Request routes to resource owner for approval within 48 hours.
3. IAM team creates account/role and documents the change ticket.
4. Onboarding checklist must include: MFA enabled, company SSO enrollment, and data-handling training completion.
Deprovisioning checklist (numbered):
1. HR flags termination/contract end.
2. Manager completes offboarding form.
3. IAM revokes access within 2 business hours for terminated employees, 24 hours for contractors.
4. Assets and secrets recovery (see data_management section).
Elevated access (break-glass):
- Criteria: emergency production access required to remediate incidents or outages.
- Process: submit break-glass request via PagerDuty with justification, 4-hour retrospective and audit log export mandatory.
SLOs & controls:
- Access request approval SLA: 48 hours.
- Quarterly entitlement review completion: 90% of owners by deadline.
- MFA enforcement: 100% of active accounts.
change_management:
Purpose: Ensure safe, auditable, and reversible changes to systems that affect availability, confidentiality, or integrity.
Change categories:
- Standard changes: pre-authorized, low-risk (e.g., routine config updates with a runbook).
- Normal changes: require change request (CR), impact assessment, scheduled window, and post-deploy verification.
- Emergency changes: expedited path for urgent fixes; retrospective review required.
Change request process (numbered):
1. Submit CR in Change Management system with: description, owner, impacted services, rollback plan, test plan, and monitoring playbook.
2. Risk assessment by service owner and security reviewer.
3. CAB (change advisory board) review for Normal changes above defined risk thresholds (see table below).
4. Schedule during approved maintenance windows and notify stakeholders 48 hours prior.
5. Execute change, monitor, and produce a post-change verification report within 24 hours.
Rollback & canary strategy:
- Mandatory rollback plan included in every Normal/Standard CR.
- Canary deploy for high-risk changes: 5% of traffic for 30 minutes before full rollout.
Risk thresholds table (plain text):
| Change type | Expected user impact | Requires CAB? | Example |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Low | None/minor | No | Config tweak for staging agent |
| Medium | Partial degradation | Yes | Database index change on low-traffic shard |
| High | Potential outage/data loss | Yes | Schema migration affecting primary DB |
Post-change auditing:
- All Normal and Emergency changes must attach change tickets to the associated incident or service record.
- Security will randomly sample 10% of changes for audit and compliance evidence each quarter.
data_management:
Data classification & handling:
- Classes: Public, Internal, Confidential, Restricted (PII/customer data).
- Storage rules: Restricted data stored in encrypted volumes only; access limited to approved roles and logged.
- Retention & deletion: Business-aligned retention schedules; automated deletion workflows for expired data.
Data lifecycle responsibilities:
- Data owner: defines classification and retention.
- Data steward: implements access and quality controls.
- Security & Compliance: enforces encryption, key management, and monitoring.
Secrets and credentials:
- Secrets must be stored in the company KMS/secret manager. Hardcoding credentials in source is prohibited.
- Rotation: service account keys rotated every 90 days; human user access keys rotated every 30 days if used.
Backups & recovery:
- Backups: nightly snapshots for production databases with 90-day retention, encrypted at rest.
- Recovery RTO/RPO: RTO 2 hours, RPO 15 minutes for core production services (listed in related_pages).
Data transfers & third-party processors:
- Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) required for processors handling Restricted data.
- Cross-border transfers: must follow data residency commitments; Security must approve exceptions.
Audit & monitoring:
- Automated DLP alerts for Restricted data exfiltration patterns.
- Quarterly data access reports delivered to Data Governance council.
procurement_and_expenses:
Procurement cadence & thresholds:
- Low-value purchases (< $2,000): Manager approval via expense system.
- Medium ($2,000–$25,000): Procurement team review and manager + finance approval.
- High (>$25,000): Procurement + finance + legal + executive approval; require a purchase order (PO).
Vendor onboarding checklist (also see vendor_management):
1. Procurement initiates RFP or quote collection.
2. Finance validates budget and payment terms.
3. Legal reviews contract and security clauses.
4. Security conducts vendor security questionnaire for vendors with system access.
Expense policies & reimbursement:
- Travel & meals: follow Corporate Travel Policy; receipts required for all reimbursements.
- Corporate cards: issued to managers and above; card limits configurable (default $5,000).
- Monthly expense reporting: expenses submitted within 30 days of spend or they may be rejected.
Compliance & record keeping:
- All procurement contracts and POs retained in the contract repository for 7 years.
- Procurement & finance run monthly invoice reconciliations; exceptions are escalated to head of Finance.
vendor_management:
Vendor risk tiers:
- Tier 1: vendors with access to production systems or Restricted data (e.g., managed infra, observability vendors).
- Tier 2: vendors with Internal data (e.g., analytics platforms).
- Tier 3: vendors with Public data only (e.g., office supplies).
Onboarding & security review (numbered):
1. Complete vendor intake form.
2. Assign vendor tier based on access and data processing.
3. Security runs a questionnaire; required penetration test or SOC2 report for Tier 1.
4. Legal finalizes contract with required SLAs and indemnities.
Ongoing vendor management:
- Quarterly performance & security reviews for Tier 1 vendors.
- Contract renewals: procurement triggers renewal review 90 days before contract end.
- Termination: offboarding checklist must include revoking credentials, confirming data return/deletion per contract, and evidence added to contract repository.
Escalation path:
- Issues escalate to Vendor Owner -> Procurement -> Security -> Legal -> Head of Finance depending on severity.
travel_policies:
Purpose: Provide safe, cost-effective travel while ensuring compliance and employee wellbeing.
Booking rules:
- Use approved travel vendors for flights and hotels.
- Economy class for flights under 6 hours; premium economy or business requires manager and People Ops approval.
- Lodging: mid-tier business hotels; exceptions require justification.
Pre-travel approvals & safety:
- Managers must approve travel with an itinerary and estimated budget in the travel system.
- Employees traveling internationally must register travel plans with People Ops and complete country risk check.
Reimbursement:
- Per diem or receipts-based reimbursement available; receipts required for all non-per-diem claims.
- Alcohol expenses reasonable and within company meal policy; lavish entertainment is not reimbursable.
Duty of care & emergency support:
- 24/7 travel support provided through the travel vendor; People Ops maintains emergency contact list and evacuation procedures for high-risk regions.
internal_templates:
Included templates (internal links):
- Access Request form (Onboarding/Offboarding).
- Change Request (CR) template with required fields and checklist.
- Vendor Intake and Risk Assessment form.
- Procurement Purchase Order (PO) template.
- Travel pre-approval and expense report templates.
How to use templates:
1. Copy the template to your project space.
2. Fill required metadata fields (owner, service, risk level).
3. Attach supporting docs (test results, quotes, security attestations).
4. Submit through the designated system or route via the documented approvers.
Template governance:
- Templates maintained by People Ops and Procurement. Suggested updates can be filed as a PR against the templates repo; changes approved monthly by the Templates working group.
